From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-05-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Compatibility policy question + exemption lanes — need clarity for comms

Team,

We have a couple of active customers (ACME and Fathom) asking for concrete language we can publish around the compatibility policy for the upcoming API/model change. Legal wants a one-paragraph customer-facing blurb and a separate internal list of allowed exemptions and criteria.

Two specific asks from me:
1) Can product confirm the acceptance window for pinned endpoints? (i.e., how long will we maintain the old model for pinned customers once we begin the cutover?)
2) Ops needs an explicit list of exemptions and the SLA change for each lane (canary, pinned, legacy).

I attached a draft compatibility matrix and a proposal for exemption lanes (very rough). I'm planning to share a short FAQ with ACME tomorrow if we have signoff.

Please reply with concrete bullets. If we need a quick sync, propose 30 minutes this afternoon.

Thanks — Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: compatibility-matrix-v1-v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-exemption-lanes.pdf (doc)

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility policy question + exemption lanes — need clarity for comms

Thanks Rishi — quick answers below based on product constraints and current roadmap: 

- Acceptance window for pinned endpoints: 90 days after GA for the new model family. After 90 days we will only support security patches on the legacy variant; functional bug fixes and performance regressions will be fixed on the new model only.

- Exemption lanes (prod suggestion):
  * "Pinned" — customer-requested retention for up to 90 days; requires a migration plan and a one-time engineering effort to port any custom hooks.
  * "Traffic-bridge" — limited runway for customers with >10k RPS or embedded devices; gated by dedicated capacity contract.
  * "Legacy-maintain" — vendor-managed, for regulated customers with audited timelines; extended on a case-by-case commercial agreement (cost + support uplift).

SLA implication: pinned and traffic-bridge customers will be on a reduced latency SLA (best-effort for old model; we guarantee throughput but not improved latency after cutover). Full SLA continues for those who migrate.

If you want more formal wording for customer comms, I can draft a one-paragraph blurb after ops confirms the SLA numbers.

M

From: ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>

Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility policy question + exemption lanes — need clarity for comms

Fwiw from CS/Customer Ops: ACME is asking explicitly whether we will provide data export tooling and whether pinned endpoints will be rate-limited during cutover. They want an SLA hedge to schedule their internal release. Recommended operational commitments: 

- Data export tool: provide a .tar of recent model cache + request logs for pinned endpoints within 7 business days (opt-in).
- Rate limits: we will not throttle pinned endpoints below their committed capacity during the 90-day window, but customers may see degraded latency for large seq lengths.

I'll coordinate with support to draft an FAQ section that covers "what to expect" during the 90 days (examples: minor behavioral diffs, prefetched KV cache will not transfer, recommended steps to test).

Ben
Principal Customer Success Manager

On a related note, ACME's procurement rep (Laura) asked for estimated costs for an extended legacy-maintain lane. We should loop finance if we go down that path.

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-23T15:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility policy question + exemption lanes — need clarity for comms

Thanks all — engineering alignment:

- We can commit to the 90-day pinned window as a policy, but operational work is required to ensure KV cache snapshots for customer migration are available. Engineering estimate: 2 full-time engineer-weeks to add an export path and validate for top-10 customers.
- For the traffic-bridge lane, we need a signed dedicated capacity contract before we promise capacity preservation. That will be a commercial + infra handoff.

I'll add a short "engineering caveats" section to the internal doc: what we can guarantee (data export timeline, no throttling below committed baseline) and what we can't (identical latency/behavior).

Lauren
Staff Engineer, Inference Platform

Adding a short legal/comms note:

- Customer-facing paragraph (draft): "Redwood will provide a 90-day compatibility window following the general availability of the new model family. During this period, customers with pinned endpoints will retain access to their legacy model for continuity while we work with them on a migration plan. Certain exempted lanes (e.g., regulated/contracted legacy-maintain customers) may be eligible for extended support under a commercial agreement. Performance characteristics may differ between legacy and new models — customers are advised to run compatibility tests and schedule migrations with Redwood support."

- We should avoid promising any performance parity language. Also recommend adding a "how to request an exemption" line with a link to a short form (we can use the existing support intake).

I'll polish the blurb into something one-sentence friendly for external comms after Lauren confirms engineering caveats.

Grace
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
